clue.text: Quarrel leading to underworld contract

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and a name for the underworld itself
a contract is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A gangland dispute ends with a hit being ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' and 'underworld' together suggest a mob killing; here they are simply two synonyms placed one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a dispute or falling-out between people, which is exactly what this noun names.

clue.text: Died suffering India's scorn

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family trees

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, damaged, so these letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A death in hardship provokes a country's contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and scorn are synonyms, both meaning a feeling of contempt for something thought unworthy.

clue.text: Vegetable in Spain served on china

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another goes above it in the grid

parts.note: Sp is a standard abbreviation for Spain or Spanish

indicators.note: food that is served has been prepared and dished up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish meal of greens is dished up on fine porcelain plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like the crockery the food is served on, but it is the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant grown and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Girl putting screen round painting

indicators.note: placing a screen round something encloses it, so the girl's name sits inside

parts.note: a grille is a grating used as a screen
Isa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman puts a screen up around a picture she is working on.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is GR(ISA)ILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisaille is a style of painting done entirely in shades of grey, often imitating sculpture.

clue.text: Finish the wrong way round

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to finish up somewhere, to arrive in the end
second meaning: stood on its end, upended, the wrong way up

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase can be a verb, to finish up, or describe something stood on end, inverted from its usual way up.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish in a particular place or state; something set end up has been turned over from normal position.

clue.text: Tower where time ran out

indicators.note: something out of order is disordered, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tower is the place where the clock stopped or the deadline expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time ran out' reads as a familiar phrase, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange the seven letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Distinguished person is apparently inefficient

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prominent or eminent individual
second meaning: read as two words, it says a person lacks capability

explanation.surface: An eminent figure turns out to be rather useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' tells you to split the word into NOT ABLE, which describes someone inefficient.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction or importance; read as 'not able' it means incapable or incompetent.

clue.text: Novel view of old statesman on modern music

parts.note: John Bright was a Victorian radical statesman and orator
taken as written
rock is a popular music style of the modern era

explanation.surface: A book presenting a Victorian politician's opinions about rock and roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'Bright on rock', as if titling the statesman's views on the music. BRIGHTON ROCK is also a stick of seaside candy sold in the English resort of Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is a 1938 novel by Graham Greene about the gangster Pinkie Brown.

clue.text: He composed grievous sins admitted by French king

indicators.note: something admitted by another is let inside it

parts.note: roi is French for king

indicators.note: grievous suggests serious harm, so the letters are damaged out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French monarch confesses to his serious wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of operas such as The Barber of Seville, so he is a man who composed.

clue.text: Signified by inserting negative in Act

indicators.note: inserting puts one item inside another, here the negative goes within the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
not is the word of negation

explanation.surface: Something was indicated by adding a refusal to a piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like a parliamentary statute, but it just means a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or indicate, so denoted and signified are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Treat alike when in ceremonial attire

parts.note: to dress a wound is to treat it
uniform means all the same, alike

explanation.surface: Everyone is handled the same way once they put on their parade clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress uniform is the formal version of military clothing worn at ceremonies and official occasions.

clue.text: TV company ran poster in Georgia

indicators.note: these words sit inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation of the US state of Georgia
taken as written
a poster is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A broadcaster put up an advertisement in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Granada Television was the ITV company serving north-west England, making shows such as Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada was a major British commercial television franchise, a company producing and broadcasting TV programmes.

clue.text: Story to make advocates turn pale outwardly

indicators.note: the colourless word is placed on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to turn the lawyers round is to read their word backwards

parts.note: the Bar is the collective term for barristers, advocates in court

explanation.surface: A tale told to make lawyers go white in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn pale' reads as a phrase meaning blanch, but 'turn' belongs with the advocates.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a simple story told to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson.

clue.text: Fish in net thrown back by companion

indicators.note: by means beside, so the companion follows on
something thrown back is sent in the opposite direction, so read the word backwards

parts.note: taken as written, before reversing
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An angler and a friend toss a catch back from the net into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown back' sounds like returning a fish to the water, which suits the angling scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family, found in European ponds and slow rivers.

clue.text: Man within the bounds of the infinite

indicators.note: within means inside, so the man goes inside the bounds

parts.note: bounds are limits
Les is a man's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: Humanity lives inside the edges of the boundless universe.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is LIMIT(LES)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infinite has no end or boundary, which is what limitless means.

clue.text: Agreeable to the ear of model upset by debts

indicators.note: by means beside, so the debts come next to it
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an IOU is a written note acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A fashion model is upset by her debts, which is welcome news to someone listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodious means tuneful and pleasant sounding, which is to say pleasing to hear.

clue.text: Forged iron panel without equal

indicators.note: forged metal is hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrought-iron panel made by a blacksmith is unmatched in quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' fits the iron perfectly as metalwork, which hides that it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil, from French, means having no match or rival, unrivalled in excellence.

clue.text: Unable to grasp point about heavenly bodies

indicators.note: grasping something holds it, so the point is taken in among the other letters
about means moved around, so all the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Someone cannot understand the significance of the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasp point' reads as understanding the argument; really the compass letter joins the other six before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are vast clouds of gas and dust in space, seen as hazy patches in the night sky.

clue.text: Hint about everybody round the formicary

indicators.note: everybody goes round, enclosing the rearranged letters

parts.note: everybody means all

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clue is passed around everyone gathered near the ants' nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A formicary is the technical word for an ants' nest, from Latin formica, meaning ant.

clue.text: Bird wearing headgear

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
something you are wearing is on you

explanation.surface: A bird is wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing headgear' is read as 'cap on', with the hat named first.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, so a domestic bird.

clue.text: Chuckle when her colt's misbehaving

indicators.note: something misbehaving does not stay in order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s being only the verb 'is'

explanation.surface: A horse owner laughs as her young horse plays up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of colt's is 'is', joining the colt to its misbehaviour; it adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to laugh gleefully, and chuckle is a close synonym for a quiet laugh.

clue.text: Demonstrate against professional being on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue being on another piece puts it above, so first in the answer

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Marching against a sports professional being tried in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to object publicly, as in a march or demonstration, against something.

clue.text: Pertaining to regular course, or part a novice followed

indicators.note: followed means coming after, so the pieces are set one behind another

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a part
taken as written
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style definition of a regular route, offering a choice about a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the regular path a body follows round another, so orbital relates to such a course.

clue.text: Instal a gantry from which to explore for ocean wreckage

indicators.note: you explore inside the run of words to find a word lying within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: Put up a crane on a ship to search the seabed for sunken cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: Lagan is a rare word for goods lying on the sea bed, often marked by a buoy for later recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagan is wreckage or cargo sunk in the sea, distinct from flotsam that floats.

clue.text: Go to sleep, being unable to hang on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to doze off, fall asleep
second meaning: to fall from something you can no longer cling to

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off because they cannot keep their grip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to nod off into slumber and to fall away when your grip fails.

clue.text: Evil monarch out for slaughter

indicators.note: the monarch sits on the outside, wrapping round the word for evil

parts.note: a king is a monarch
ill can mean evil or harmful, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A wicked ruler sets out to massacre his people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out for' reads as intent on, but 'out' puts the monarch outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A killing is an act of slaughter, the taking of life.

clue.text: The "last longer" overall?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to endure beyond, to outlast
second meaning: as a noun, clothing worn over the rest, an overall

explanation.walkthrough: 'overall' looks like an adverb meaning in total; it is the protective coat worn over other clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear is to outlast in use, and outerwear or an outwear garment is one worn outside like an overall.

clue.text: Carry out sole test needed to adapt to new conditions?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: touching the bottoms of your own lower limbs to check them
second meaning: the idiom for growing confident in an unfamiliar situation

explanation.surface: Checking the soles of your feet is necessary to settle into a new place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the fish or 'only', but it is the underside of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to gain confidence and settle in, becoming used to a new job or situation.
